fixture_assessment.why: Only the LAS and its ASCII twin are in portable, open formats a non-IP tool can read. The .las is a compact (2249 rows, 14 curves) quad/triple-combo openhole set (CALI, RHOB, TNPH, SP, SGR, LLD/LLS/MSFLC, DTLN, DRHO) WITH interleaved core perm/porosity/grain-density - enough to regression-test Vsh, PHIE, Archie/shaly-sand Sw, and a log-core crossplot end to end.
regression_value: LAS-reader stress fixture: WRAP=YES multi-line records, non-standard '~P' parameter section, -999 nulls, mixed log+discrete-core sampling
ASCII-import parity fixture: Testdata.txt must decode to identical arrays as Testdata.las
Quicklook FE fixture: full openhole triple/quad combo + core calibration points
IP well-parameter block (RW/RMF/RMC + temps + KB/DF/GL/datum) as an example of IP's ~P defaults

license_flag.detail: All TestData ships inside a licensed PGL / Lloyd's Register / Geoactive IP 2025 install and is governed by the IP EULA. Content is SYNTHETIC/fictitious (Test Well 1 / 'Somewhere' / North Sea; PGL as company) so it carries no third-party field confidentiality, but the sample files themselves may still be vendor-owned. Before bundling Testdata.las/.txt into the SandiBumi repo, confirm the IP EULA permits redistribution of sample data, OR regenerate an equivalent synthetic LAS in-house.
license_flag.contrast_with_techlog: Cleaner licensing question than Techlog's fixtures but weaker provenance: SLB Techlog shipped a REAL Indonesian field set (BLSO Balam South, LAPI 2023, 36 LAS) usable as genuine field fixtures once client-cleared; IP ships one SYNTHETIC vendor demo LAS.

calibration_vs_techlog.techlog_ingest: 38 files / 36 LAS = a real multi-well field dataset (Balam South 'BLSO', LAPI-2023 reprocessing, with TLFamily_* processed curves, TVDSS, FTEMP_BLSO). Directly usable as import + regression fixtures.
calibration_vs_techlog.ip_ingest: 9 files but effectively ONE portable synthetic well (Testdata.las) + its .txt twin; 3 opaque IP-native DB wells; 1 binary project; 2 WITSML realtime demo files.
comparison: Volume: Techlog >> IP (36 real LAS vs 1 synthetic LAS).
Portability: both ship LAS; IP adds an opaque native .dat DB that Techlog's sample set did not rely on.
Provenance: Techlog = real field (Indonesian, Mahakam-relevant); IP = synthetic North-Sea-flavoured demo.
IP unique extras: an IP '~P' parameter section inside LAS and a WITSML realtime config - neither present in the Techlog LAS set.

Net: for SandiBumi fixtures the Techlog BLSO set remains the stronger regression corpus; IP's Testdata.las is a good SECONDARY LAS-parser + quicklook fixture, especially for WRAP=YES and '~P' handling.
